Introduction

What Is a One Person Company?

A One Person Company is a company structure introduced under the Companies Act, 2013, that lets a single individual own and run a company with limited liability. It's a separate legal entity from its owner, unlike a Proprietorship, while avoiding the requirement for a second shareholder that a Private Limited Company needs.

It's a natural fit for solo founders who want the credibility and liability protection of a company structure without bringing in a co-founder purely to satisfy a shareholder requirement.

Weigh Your Options

Advantages & Disadvantages

Advantages

  • Limited liability protection for the sole owner
  • Separate legal entity distinct from the individual founder
  • No requirement to find a second shareholder
  • Greater credibility with banks and vendors than a Proprietorship
  • Perpetual succession via a mandatory nominee

Disadvantages

  • Cannot have more than one member — limits certain funding options
  • Mandatory conversion to a Private/Public company beyond prescribed turnover or capital thresholds
  • Higher compliance than a Proprietorship, including annual ROC filings
  • A resident nominee must be appointed at incorporation

Eligibility

Who Can Register an OPC

  • Only one member, who must be an Indian citizen and resident
  • A resident nominee must be appointed at the time of incorporation
  • One director minimum (the sole member can also be the director)
  • A registered office address in India
  • Not eligible for entities carrying out certain financial activities restricted for OPCs

Step-by-Step

Registration Process & Timeline

1. Digital Signature Certificate (DSC)

Obtain DSC for the sole member/director — typically 1 working day.

2. Name Reservation

Apply for company name approval, including the mandatory "OPC" suffix — 1 to 2 working days.

3. Nominee Consent

Obtain written consent (Form INC-3) from the nominee who will take over in case of the member's death or incapacity.

4. SPICe+ Filing

Incorporation application filed with the ROC along with the nominee's consent and other required forms.

5. Certificate of Incorporation

Once approved, you receive the Certificate of Incorporation, PAN and TAN — typically within 10–15 working days overall. Timelines can vary.

Required Documents

What You'll Need

  • PAN card of the member and nominee
  • Aadhaar / address proof of the member and nominee
  • Passport-size photographs
  • Proof of registered office (utility bill + NOC from owner)
  • Nominee's written consent (Form INC-3)

Annual Compliance

Ongoing Requirements After Registration

  • Annual ROC filing (AOC-4 & MGT-7A)
  • Statutory audit of financial statements
  • Income tax return filing
  • At least one board meeting in each half of the calendar year
  • Director KYC (DIR-3 KYC)

Post-Registration Requirements

Immediately After Incorporation

  • Open a current bank account in the company's name
  • Deposit subscribed share capital
  • Apply for GST registration, if applicable
  • Appoint the first statutory auditor within 30 days
  • Monitor turnover and capital thresholds that trigger mandatory conversion
